model.name: tailwindcss
model.description:
# Figma to Tailwind CSS v4 Theme


A Dev Mode codegen plugin that extracts Figma variables and converts them to Tailwind CSS v4 `@theme` format.


## Features


🎨 **Colors** — Automatically converted to `oklch` for better color manipulation


📏 **Spacing & Sizing** — Proper unit conversion to rem/px


🔲 **Borders** — Radius and border widths


🌑 **Shadows** — Box shadows, drop shadows, inset shadows


✍️ **Typography** — Font families, sizes, weights, line heights, letter spacing


⚡ **Motion** — Durations, easing functions, animations


📱 **Layout** — Breakpoints, containers, aspect ratios


🎯 **Utility-specific colors** — Control which utilities a color generates (bg-*, text-*, border-*)


## How It Works


Name your Figma variables with a namespace prefix like `color/primary`, `spacing/lg`, or `radius/md`. The plugin converts them to Tailwind CSS variables like `--color-primary`, `--spacing-lg`, `--radius-md`.


Tailwind v4 automatically generates utility classes from these variables—no configuration needed.

model.name: Sync Variables with Notion
model.description:
Synchronizes variables from a Notion database to a Figma document's Variable Collection. This is particularly useful for managing application text in Notion or supporting multiple languages.


🔥 How to use


Sync collection tab

Connects a Notion database to a Figma Variable Collection and synchronizes their values. Settings are saved per Figma document.


1. Database ID

Specify the Notion database ID (Reference).


2. Integration token

First, create a new integration in Notion (Reference). Next, grant your integration page permissions (Reference). Enter the copied token.


3. Key property name

Specify the name of the Notion property that serves as the unique key for the variables (e.g., Name, Key, ID). Currently, title, formula, and text properties are supported as keys.


4. Collection name to create or update

Specify the name of the Figma Variable Collection to sync with. Existing local collection names will be suggested via autocomplete. If the specified collection doesn't exist, it will be created.


5. Add or reorder modes

Specify the Notion property names that correspond to Figma Variable Modes. These properties will hold the variable values for each mode (e.g., language).


  1. Adding modes:
  2. Enter a mode name in the textbox (e.g., ja, en, or other property names in your Notion database).
  3. Click the "Add" button to add it to the list.
  4. Reordering modes: Modes in the list can be reordered via drag and drop. This order will be reflected in the order of Figma variable modes.
  5. Removing modes: Click the X icon to the right of each mode name to remove that mode from the list.


After entering the information for steps 1-4, click the "Sync variable collection with Notion" button to start the synchronization. This process might take some time depending on the number of items in the database and the variables.


List tab

About list tab

Displays variables from the selected Collection. Only STRING type variables applicable to TEXT_CONTENT are shown. You can copy keys and values, and filter the list by key or value. Clicking on a row reveals the button described below.


"Apply variable to selected text" button

Select text layers in Figma and click the button to apply the variable.


Display mode

Select the Variable Mode (e.g., language) to display its corresponding values in the list.


About caching

When the target collection is a library collection, this plugin caches its information in client storage. This is done because fetching library collections with many variables can be time-consuming and might hit Figma's API rate limits. Clicking the "Refresh" button clears the cache and fetches the latest variable data.


Utilities tab

Provides several utility actions to help manage variables and their application to text layers.


Target collection

Select the Variable Collection to target for the actions. You can choose a collection or all collections.


Target text range

Select the scope for the actions: "Selection", "Current page", or "All pages". You can also choose whether to include text layers within components ("Include text within components") or instances ("Include text within instances") using the respective checkboxes.


Limit variable name

Optionally, enter text here to limit the "Bulk apply variables" action to only those variables whose names contain the specified text.


"Bulk apply variables" button

Automatically applies variables to text layers within the selected range. It matches text content with variable values across all modes in the target collection(s).


"Highlight applied variables" button

Visualizes variable usage on text layers. Text layers with variables applied are highlighted in blue, while those without are highlighted in red.


📮 Support

If you have any problems or feedback, please use the GitHub Issues.


===


This plugin was created by Ryo Nakae 🙎‍♂️.


https://brdr.jp

https://x.com/ryo_dg

https://github.com/ryonakae

model.name: CodeFig
model.description:
CodeFig is a script runner for Figma, inspired by the Scripter plugin by @rsms.

It comes with a curated set of utility scripts covering framing and auto-layout, style and variable batch operations, design-system foundations (grid, typography, spacing, corner radius), and small workflow helpers (e.g. annotations from comments).


Variables are supported as a first-class use case, but CodeFig is intentionally broader than variable tooling.


Scripts run as plain JavaScript in the Figma plugin sandbox.


---


Scripts:



Utility Scripts


Comments to annotations

Reads Figma comments via the REST API and converts them into annotations.

Useful when duplicating designs across files, as comments don’t carry over. The script preserves comment positions by creating hidden anchors (since comments are usually attached to the root frame, not individual elements). REQUIRES READ COMMENTS API TOKEN


Detach styles & variables

Removes style and/or variable bindings from the current selection. You can choose which types to detach (fill, stroke, effect, typography, etc.) or remove all bindings.


Duplicate styles group

Duplicate a styles group, with optionally rebinding its variable bindings to another collection.


Duplicate variable collection

Duplicates a variable collection with its metadata and values.


Frame or auto layout selected

Wraps (on unwraps) each selected layers in new frames or auto-layout containers individually.


Remove unnecessary nesting

Detects and removes redundant wrapper frames (e.g. wrappers with only one child). Optionally normalizes wrappers (e.g. combining padding-x on wrapper 1 and padding-y on wrapper 2 into a single wrapper).


Rename styles

Batch-renames styles using find/replace rules, similar to Figma’s batch rename.


Rename variables

Batch-renames variables using find/replace rules, similar to Figma’s batch rename.


Render styles overview

Generates a visual overview of a defined style group in a frame.

Primarily used to support Replace Styles, which requires all styles to exist in the file. The easiest approach is to generate the overview in the library file and paste it into the target file.


Replace style variable bindings

Batch find and replaces variable bindings inside style definitions.


Replace styles

Batch finds and rebinds node style assignments to different styles based on name matching and the local style inventory. Style replacement is less smooth than with variables due to limited Figma styles API support, so it requires a two-step approach.


Replace variables

Batch finds and rebinds layer variable references or collections to another.


Scale or resize elements

Scales or resizes selected nodes by factor, ratio, or explicit dimensions (e.g. resize all selected to 16:9 with a width of 640px).


Select by styles or variables

Selects all nodes that use a specific style or variable.


Text to styles

Creates text styles from selected text layers, keeping variable bindings (if there is any).


Variable inspector (WIP)

Inspects variable bindings and usage details in the file or selection. The goal is to find broken or outdated bindings and disconnected library artifacts. Still in progress due to the complexity.



Design System Foundations

These enable you to create a highly configurable design system foundation, with as many breakpoints as needed, and to optimize spacing, grid, typography, and corner radius per breakpoint.


Corner radius

Creates or updates corner radius variables across breakpoint modes and sets their respective scopes. Highly configurable: set min–max values and define as many steps, increment types, and naming conventions as needed.


Grid

Creates or updates layout grid variables across breakpoint modes, sets their respective scopes, creates a grid styles for the setup, and generates preview frames with the grid setup.


Spacing

Creates or updates spacing variables across breakpoint modes and sets their respective scopes. Highly configurable: set min–max values per breakpoint and define as many steps, increment types, and naming conventions as needed.


Typography

Creates or updates typography variables across breakpoint modes with their respective scopes. and optionally matching text styles. Highly configurable: set min–max values per breakpoint and define as many steps, increment types, and naming conventions as needed.



Importable Libraries


@Core Library

General utility helpers for node traversal, styles, colors, and shared low-level operations.


@CodeFigUI

Helpers for building script config UIs inside CodeFig.


@InfoPanel

Utilities for showing structured results in the plugin UI.


@Math Helpers

Math and scaling helpers for interpolation, easing, ratios, and generated scales.


@Pattern Matching

Shared pattern and wildcard matching utilities.


@Replacement Engine

Core logic for planning and applying find/replace operations.


@Styles

Helpers for discovering, analyzing, and replacing styles.


@Variables

Helpers for collections, variables, bindings, and value updates.


---

Support the development if you like:

https://www.buymeacoffee.com/codefig


MIT — free for commercial and non-commercial use.

Built for the Figma community.

https://github.com/marxcie/CodeFig

model.name: Source DS Utils
model.description:
Bunch of utilities for Source Design System and Source Foundation plugin. I feel like these automations can be useful for everyone who designs in Figma.


This is a UI-less plugin that uses Figma quick actions to run automations.


Export component templates

Select components or frames with components and run the command to copy all these components as frames. You can use these copies to import component templates back.


Import component templates

Select a frame with exported component templates and run the command. This command will either replace target component content with the contents of the template or it will merge layers


Fix layers

Sometimes Figma does not resize absolutely positioned layers when you update something rapidly. When you spot such rouge layers went off you can fix them with this automation.


This command finds all absolutely positioned layers inside auto layout frames and snaps their size back to fit the parent.


Create color Styles

This command will create colour styles that are bound to the variables of the same name.


Clone component

Effortlessly clone any component or component set. When you copy/paste a simple component with lots of properties Figma creates a component instance. This automation creates an identical copy with all the properties available.


Make local component

Simplify workflow for slot components. This automation takes the instance inside another component, creates a local copy of that instance, makes it a component and swaps it with that component.


Slot to local component

Simplify workflow for slot components. This automation takes the instance, checks instance swap properties and enables you to swap it with newly created component. Lear more here -> https://forum.figma.com/t/slot-component-workflow-plugin/93749


Update Elevation Components

This is Source Design System specific automation. It reads effect styles and updates custom-made elevation components to match effect shadows.


Set Playground

Mark any file as Source Foundation Playground. This plugin uses figma.root.setPluginData method from plugin API to toggle 'SDSPlayground' property.

Oklch Engine fixes this by offering the industry's first dual-mode workstation:


🚀 KEY FEATURES:

• Dev Export Engine: Copy production-ready code blocks directly to clipboard for Tailwind CSS config, CSS variables, SwiftUI, and Android Compose.

• Variables Export: Save your generated scales directly into Figma Native Variables or document swatches with one click.


5. DESIGNER WORKFLOW UTILITIES

• Pinned Swatches: Saved history swatches that persist locally on your system between plugin sessions.

model.name: RSe Toolbox
model.description:
RSe Toolbox is a set of utilities for keeping design systems and component libraries in shape finds variables and instances, inspects layers, and exports data for documentation or code.


FUNCTIONS

• **Variables used** - counts how many times each local variable is used, and where.

• **Components used** - counts instances per component, split into direct vs. inherited.

• **Find Component Instances** - finds every instance of the selected component or variant set.

• **Analyze Layer** - lists every visual attribute (fills, effects, typography, etc.) in a selected layer, flagging variables vs. styles vs. hardcoded values.

• **Get Texts** - pulls all text content out of a selection

• **Get HTML** - exports a selection as HTML + CSS

• **Get Structure** - exports a JSON tree of every component instance inside a selection, with its properties

• **Detach All** - detaches an instance and everything nested inside it


No data leaves Figma — everything runs locally in the plugin, no network access.

Generate WCAG-compliant color palettes from a single seed color. DesignAlly creates accessible light & dark themes, checks contrast ratios against AA/AAA standards, and previews colors on real UI patterns — buttons, cards, forms, tables, and nav. Simulate vision impairments (protanopia, deuteranopia, tritanopia, low vision) to stress-test your palette. DesignAlly — Accessible Color Palettes in One Click


Stop struggling with manual contrast checks and guesswork. DesignAlly generates complete, WCAG-compliant color palettes from a single seed color — light and dark mode, ready to use.


How it works


Pick a seed color, choose a style (Modern, Minimal, Vibrant, or Soft), set your contrast target (AA/AAA), and DesignAlly produces a full 42-color palette instantly. Every color is computed using Material Color Utilities and adjusted for accessibility automatically.


Features


- One-click generation — 42 accessible colors from any seed

model.name: Design to NativeWind
model.description:
Design to NativeWind turns a selected frame into a React Native + NativeWind component.


It runs as a Dev Mode code generator: pick a layer and it emits a typed component built from react-native primitives and NativeWind utility classes. The conversion is rule-based and deterministic — the same design always produces the same code.


What it converts:


- Auto Layout into flex direction, alignment, gap, and padding

- Sizing (fill / hug / fixed) into width and height classes

- Fills, corner radius, opacity, and typography

- Vector layers into react-native-svg

- Repeated subtrees hoisted into reusable sub-components

- Imported Tailwind config or CSS theme tokens, mapped to color and spacing utilities


Spacing and radius snap to the nearest Tailwind scale step within a tolerance you choose (strict / default / loose), and fall back to an arbitrary value when nothing fits.


Optional LLM cleanup:


Running the plugin (outside Dev Mode codegen) opens a panel where you can paste an Anthropic API key to refine component and variable names. It is off by default and never changes the visual result.


Privacy and network access:


The plugin works fully offline by default. The only network request is the optional LLM cleanup. When you enable it and provide your own Anthropic API key, the selected design's structure and the generated code are sent to the Anthropic API (api.anthropic.com) to improve naming. Your API key is stored locally in Figma client storage and is sent only to Anthropic. The plugin author does not collect, store, or transmit your data anywhere else.
model.tagline: Convert a Figma selection into React Native + NativeWind code.

model.name: Toolkit
model.description:
Toolkit is a set of everyday design utilities in one plugin. Open it, pick a tool, get the job done.


TOOLS INCLUDED


PixelPort - Lossless Import

Bring big images and PDFs into Figma at full resolution. Figma downscales anything over 4096px on its longest edge a 2560x9529 screenshot becomes 1100x4096 and loses most of its detail. PixelPort auto-tiles the image into slices under the limit and reassembles them, so every pixel is preserved. Import PNG, JPG, WEBP, GIF and PDF; multi-file; PDFs page by page at your DPI.


Font Swapper - Find, review & replace fonts

Scan a frame, page, or the whole file to see every font in use, where and how much. Replace a whole family (styles mapped automatically) or a single style, with a live preview. Catches fonts inside mixed-font layers, flags missing fonts, and locates usage across pages. Never silently substitutes a weight.


Color Swap - Find & replace colors

Scan for every solid color in use, then swap it for another color, a Figma variable, or a paint style. Locate where a color is used, spot near-duplicates and raw-vs-tokenized colors, and clean up your palette. Undoable.


Iconry - Browse & import icons

Browse the open-source icon set and import icons as reusable component sets, auto-sorted by category on a tidy library page. Restyle by size and color, bind to a variable, and drag icons straight onto your canvas.


PRIVACY

PixelPort, Font Swapper and Color Swap process everything locally on your device. Iconry fetches icon SVGs from the public jsDelivr CDN so you can browse and import them; no design data is ever sent anywhere.


Icons: Tabler (MIT).
model.tagline: Import losslessly, swap fonts & colors, and add icons — all in one plugin.

Lineaworks Tools provides two core utilities for Figma production work.

Image Mask — Quickly wrap image nodes into clipped frames with custom dimensions, corner radius (including circle), and 9-point anchor control. Supports Figma Variables for radius tokens and batch processing.

Layer Sort — Reorder selected layers by their canvas position (top-to-bottom or left-to-right) or reverse the current order, keeping your layer panel clean and logical.

model.name: Omnius
model.description:
A collection of utilities I use when starting a new project.


Pasterino

Sticky notes pasting.


Colorino

Pulls the latest OKLCH colors palette from Tailwind, converts it to sRGB, and creates variable set plus an overview page.


Typerino

Fonts' glyphs are drawn from a specific starting point used as a base size. Depending on that, some font size values may result in the text being vertically off-center when placed within a container. Typerino analyzes the font used at the selected text layer to provide the sizes which would result in a perfect vertical alignment.


Baserino

There are many fonts whose vertical baseline position is shifted out of the box resulting in a text looking vertically misaligned when used within a container. Baserino fixes that.


Cornerino

Automatic corner smoothing to specified value across the file.


Vectorino

Flattens the shapes correctly without Figma's typical extra anchors and glitches.


Iconerino

Assembles a workspace inside Figma to work on the app icons, and then exports them in a build-friendly way.


There might be more tools to come. Or not.
